_comment: HDSP Worker service — Phase 9, Task 9.2/9.6. Identical image to hdsp-api (same backend.Dockerfile build), distinguished only by PROCESS_ROLE=worker below. Sized per the 'Small (pilot)' tier (1 task) from HDSP_Cloud_Migration_Architecture_Review.md Section 17. NOT attached to the ALB -- see infrastructure/terraform/alb.tf, which only targets hdsp-api and hdsp-frontend.
_scaling_note: Keep desiredCount=1 until a distributed lock is added for the in-process @Cron jobs (password-reset expiry, campaign scheduler, token daily reset/analytics, CMS cleanup -- Phase 8 Task 8.6's tenant-iterated jobs). Scaling this service beyond 1 task reintroduces the exact duplicate-tick risk PROCESS_ROLE=api was built to avoid on the API tier (see HDSP_Cloud_Migration_Architecture_Review.md's 'second replica would double-process every tick' finding) -- @nestjs/schedule has no built-in distributed lock. Bull queue consumers (NotificationProcessor, AuditProcessor, etc.) ARE safe to scale beyond 1 task -- Bull's per-job Redis lock already handles concurrent consumers correctly; only the cron side is the constraint on this task's desiredCount.

containerDefinitions.name: hdsp-worker
containerDefinitions._health_check_note: No HTTP healthCheck block -- PROCESS_ROLE=worker never calls app.listen() (see main.ts), so there is no port to probe. ECS falls back to container-status (is the process alive) for this task definition; if deeper liveness is needed later, add a lightweight TCP or file-touch heartbeat, not an HTTP endpoint that would require standing up a second listener just for this.

_service_notes: ECS service: desiredCount=1 (see _scaling_note above), NOT registered with any ALB target group, deploymentConfiguration.minimumHealthyPercent=0/maximumPercent=200 acceptable here (brief queue/cron processing gap during deploy is tolerable, unlike API request-serving downtime).
